suite.doc:
UAT: MicroVMImage Governance — validates AWS ARN collision prevention.
AWS Lambda MicroVM image ARNs are identified by name within a single AWS account and region — they have no concept of Kubernetes namespaces. Two MicroVMImage CRs with the same metadata.name in different namespaces would silently resolve to the same AWS ARN, and deleting one while the other's MicroVMs are still running causes AWS to permanently reject the delete, leaving the deleting namespace stuck Terminating indefinitely. See docs/design/image-arn-collision-prevention.md (KubeMicroVM Community) for the full root-cause analysis.
IMG-01: Duplicate-named MicroVMImage in a second namespace is rejected by the validating webhook at kubectl apply time. IMG-02: The sanctioned PRO cross-namespace imageRef + MicroVMImageBinding path is unaffected by the collision check — a consumer namespace can still reference a catalog image without creating its own MicroVMImage. IMG-03: Deleting a MicroVMImage while another namespace's MicroVMs still reference it produces a DeleteBlocked Kubernetes Event and a bounded (not unbounded) retry count, without ever removing the finalizer.
